Zod 4 accepts a `.refine()`d ZodObject as a discriminatedUnion member — verified in this workspace against zod 4.3.6: the union routed `phase: "test"` to the refined member and reported `proof: custom a passing test handoff needs the tester's own proof`. docs/solutions/daemon/handoff-schema-migration-patterns.md says a `.transform()` member becomes ZodEffects and is rejected — that was Zod 3. newSection: ## When no surface reaches the changed path
No surface reaches the changed path is a report to the architect, never a reason to complete the phase.
Say which surface is missing and what it would have to do — a rig that can spawn the role, a
sandbox that holds the resource, a credential, a command that does not exist yet — and send it to

infrastructure, we need to fix it; if it's tooling, we need to develop it; if it's skills, we need
to fix the skills." A code path whose first execution would be after the merge — a deploy
workflow's inline step, a post-merge helper, a production-only resource — is untested until you
have executed it somewhere production-like; completing with a unit-test-only handoff is the
failure this rule exists to stop.

The rig's inert root architect never registers, so its per-tree registration deadline would retire and relaunch it and, at MAX_LAUNCH_FAILURES, mark the tree `launch-failed` — which revokes the architect capability the driver is using. `worker_boot_timeout_seconds: 900` keeps that out of a 20-minute run; if a run goes long, re-read `state.json` and re-do `/process/started` on the current generation.
Each pane costs about 450 MB. Five workers plus the inert root and controller is roughly 3 GB; check free memory before the run and keep `worker_cap: 6`.

The rig's plugin-tree copy is ~240 MB and is reused across runs; `RIG_REFRESH_PLUGINS=1` re-copies. `setup.sh` refuses (exit 2) if the rig profile and the source profile resolve to the same directory — never pass `RIG_PROFILE=legion`.

A credentialed command (`legion gh`, `jj git push`, `legion handoff complete`) must be first in its own bash call: the grant lives 60 seconds from the start of the call (worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md section 1).
After `jj split`, the issue bookmark sits on the empty working copy; move it with `jj bookmark set legion/LEGION-53 -r @- --allow-backwards` before pushing (worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md section 3).
ordering: Strictly sequential, one implementer. Task 1 -> Task 2 -> Task 3, each its own commit, because Task 2 consumes Task 1's exported formatter and Tasks 1 and 2 both touch ledger.test.ts and cli/handoff.test.ts (jj path scoping is all-or-nothing per file, so the edits must be sequenced between splits). Then: open the PR with the `E2E (implementer)` line already filled from the Task-1/2 proofs, run the rig for acceptance 3 and 4 before reporting completion, and add the rig's proof to `.legion/implement.json` and the PR body.
